o: Each round Alice removes the current minimum, Bob removes the next minimum; Bob appends his first, then Alice — so each round appends (second-smallest, smallest) of the remainder. This is exactly: sort ascending, then swap each adjacent pair. [5,4,2,3] sorts to [2,3,4,5] and swaps to [3,2,5,4], matching the example.
k: The game simulates repeatedly extracting the two minima.
Result = sorted array with each adjacent pair swapped.

a.n: Approach 1: Sort and swap adjacent pairs
a.i: Sorting reproduces the removal order; appending Bob's pick before Alice's swaps each consecutive pair. One sort plus one pass.
s: For i = 0, 2, 4, … swap nums[i] and nums[i+1].
a.t: O(n log n) — dominated by sorting.
a.sp: O(1) extra space (in-place sort and swaps).

w: Always give the sort-and-swap insight first — it turns a simulation into one line of reasoning. Pitfall: the append order is Bob-first, i.e., larger of the pair first within each round.
